slides.title: Measuring the Motor's Speed
slides.subtitle: ENGS 28 · Day 12 — In-Class

slides.title: Where we are
items: On Wednesday we worked through TTmotor_ramp.c one register at a time.
In the reading you worked out how to turn a count of pulses from the speed sensor into revolutions per minute.
Today we'll wire that sensor, look at its output on the oscilloscope, and then build the rest of the Lab 6 system with the measurement in it.

Where you are, and what is left
items: You have the speed sensor wired, its pulses on the oscilloscope, and the arithmetic that turns them into revolutions per minute.
For Lab 6: the tb6612 driver, the potentiometer mapped to a mode and a speed, the pulse counter on PA15, and the rpm on the display.
The optional experiment at the end of the lab is the 50 Hz one: run the PWM at 50 Hz instead of 1.6 kHz and listen to the motor.
